messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted API queue length crossing critical threshold in us-west-2 (metric: hosted.request_queue.size > 15k) — p95 latency spike detected. auto-page oncall.
ashley: I'm on it. seeing a big backlog on /v1/generate — p95 ~1200ms p99 ~8.3s and 504s creeping up. queue ~18,432 and still climbing. paging SRE and infra.
maya: @ashley oncall here, grabbing pager. any evidence of model OOMs or just provisioner failure?
dashley: not OOMs — GPUs are saturated and autoscaler not launching new nodes. provisioner logs show repeated 429s from cloud API (quota limit). suspect provisioner has hit rate/instance quota.
priya: dropping in. can you paste the top lines from the provisioner leader logs?
ashley: paste: ```
2026-03-15T18:03:42Z provisioner leader: request_node_create -> cloud_api error 429 QuotaExceeded: quota 'GPUs per project' exceeded
2026-03-15T18:03:44Z provisioner: retry backoff 30s
2026-03-15T18:04:10Z autoscaler: desired_scale=120 current=98 pending=0
2026-03-15T18:04:12Z provisioner: throttled by rate limiter: 100 req/min
```
leo: Confirmed cloud quota at project level is exhausted for this region — we've consumed burst capacity earlier today from a training job. I can open emergency quota request but time to approve is uncertain.
ops-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hosted-backlog-provisioner.md — recommended mitigations: 1) enable degraded routing, 2) throttle non-SLAs, 3) warm small-model pool, 4) manual eviction of idle sessions.
sre-runbook-bot: Suggest starting with throttling and degraded routing immediately. Manual eviction command: `scripts/evict_idle_sessions --age 600 --region us-west-2` (use with caution).
ashley: Doing manual evict now (running as one-off): ```
$ scripts/evict_idle_sessions --age 600 --region us-west-2
Evicted 1423 sessions, freed 64 active GPU slots
```
ashley: queue dropped by ~1200 after that but still climbing, autoscaler still cannot create because cloud quota 0 left.
priya: I'm switching routing for low-priority traffic to cpu-fallback lane (best-effort, higher latency) — will reduce GPU load for premium clients. Applying policy now.
priya: policy applied: `route:if(client_tags contains 'low-priority') -> fallback:cpu-line` — waiting on metrics.
ashley: p95 improved to 950ms for premium routes but total queue still ~14,900. we need more capacity or cut heavier clients.
dan: I'm going to restart the provisioner leader to clear potential deadlocks with rate limiter token bucket — restarting now.
dan: ```
systemctl restart provisioner-leader
# tail -n 50 /var/log/provisioner/leader.log
```
dan: leader came back but immediately logs cloud 429. restart didn't help; this is quota-level.
leo: I've opened emergency quota ticket with cloud provider (case #CL-88921). Also requested temporary quota raise for GPUs in us-west-2. ETA unknown but flagged urgent.
support-bot: Support triage: two customers reported timeouts on generative endpoint (Customer A and Customer B). Customer A SLA-impacting errors at 1.8% of requests in last 10m. Customer notifications queued.
maya: Customer impact summary: 1) Premium clients mostly serving via degraded routing now — best effort latencies but functional. 2) Non-SLA clients receiving CPU-fallback or 503s depending on policy. 3) Observed spike originated from a third-party partner hitting our API with unthrottled batch infer requests around 17:58UTC.
ashley: Can we add a rate limit override to the partner to throttle them immediately?
priya: I can add a temporary rate-limit rule per api-key: `api.rate_limit[partner-x] = 10r/s` — applying.
priya: rule deployed, will watch.
ashley: metrics: after throttling and evictions: queue 11,200 -> p95 650ms p99 3.1s. error rate down to 0.9% but still elevated.
leo: While quota is pending, we should enable two mitigations: 1) spin up a small warm pool of quantized T4-like instances from a cold pool if provider allows (cheaper SKU), 2) continue customer throttles. I've started a request to provision alternate GPU SKUs.
maya: Can we also enable model fallback to quantized-small for non-critical completions? that'll cut GPU memory and allow more concurrency.
priya: enabling model-family fallback for low-priority routes: `model_fallback: [redwood-small-q8, redwood-small-q4]` — done.
ashley: ops note: we've enabled degraded routing, manual evictions done, partner throttled, model fallback enabled, and CPU-fallback for low-priority clients. Still waiting on cloud quota.
support-bot: Notifying customers: drafted message to Customer A/B explaining partial degradation and mitigation steps. (Will send after approvals.)
leo: Cloud expressed they saw the quota request and escalated to their infra team — no firm ETA but they marked as high priority.
maya: Handoff: I'm taking incident for the night shift. Summary for next oncall: current queue ~9,400 and slowly trending down, active autoscaler attempts blocked by provider quota, mitigation in place: degraded routing, partner throttled, evictions done, model fallbacks enabled. Open action items: 1) follow cloud quota case (leo), 2) monitor p99 and queue length and escalate if queue > 12k, 3) prepare rollback plan if degraded routing causes quality regressions.
maya: tagging SRE-rotation oncall for visibility and asking product for any business-side comms if quota delay >2h.
ashley: thanks team — leaving notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/6412349876 — will join async for RCA tomorrow.
inc-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03015-6412349876 — severity=high, impact=degraded_serving_for_non_sla_clients, current_state=mitigated
maya: copying timeline and runbook updates into the incident doc now. ping me if any regression.
